text:
sanjay: incident-bot just opened a PD flood for 'inference-p99-latency' across us-east-1. paging spike ~3x baseline, lots of duplicates. looks noisy but some customers are seeing real timeouts. kicking off live mitigation.

incident-bot: ALERT: inference-p99-latency (service=runtime) triggered 82 times in 5m. paging: pagerduty-critical. link: https://monitoring/redwood/alerts/1955556789 :rotating_light:

leah: on it. can someone check whether this correlates with the model rollout from this morning? i saw a canary that finished at 08:12.

maria: i can check canary. quick grep shows canary model v2.3 deployed at 08:11 to a subset of pods, but rollout policy shouldn't have affected us-east primary pool. searching logs now.

alex: i'm looking at the serving nodes — cpu ok, gpu mem fine, but queue length across the frontends jumped. a lot of small requests spiking concurrent connections. could be upstream retry storm.

leah: ok mitigation suggestions: 1) temporary PD routing to 'oncall-rotation' only 2) enable dedupe window 300s for this alert 3) add a short-term rate-limit on alert channel so Slack doesn't spam everyone. anyone object?

sanjay: +1 to all. add: switch grouping key to (customer_id, route) instead of instance for the next 15m to reduce duplicate PD incidents for the same customer.

maria: i'll create a quick dashboard slice: p99 by customer and route, 15m window. will post link.

alex: i can flip the alert dedupe policy in Alert Manager. plan: increase dedupe window to 300s, set grouping labels to customer_id,route, and add a temporary suppression rule for low-traffic backend errors. executing now.

incident-bot: ACTION: Alert Manager updated by alex. dedupe_window=300s, grouping_labels=[customer_id,route], suppression: error_type in (misrouted-429) for 10m.

leah: i pushed a short-term PD routing change — only paging the oncall-rotation group and mobile-sdk leads. link to PD rule: https://pagerduty/rules/65432. also muted noisy slack channel alerts for #infra-alerts for 20m.

maria: dashboard: https://grafana/redwood/d/abcd/inference-noise-sweep?from=-15m&to=now — p99 spike concentrated on customer: fintech-ops and route: /v1/generate. looks like high retry rate from their client.

sanjay: good catch. we should reach out to fintech-ops SREs through their escalation channel but avoid full PD until they confirm. who wants to message them?

alex: i'll DM their oncall. quick template: "we're seeing elevated p99s for /v1/generate tied to high concurrent retries from your client. can you confirm recent config changes?"

leah: while we wait, let's enable adaptive thresholding for that route: raise the p99 threshold 20% for 30m so we don't keep paging for borderline issues while we confirm impact. can product/observability follow up with a post-incident evaluation?

maria: agreed on adaptive threshold. i'll open a follow-up ticket to run the post-incident alert sweep and propose permanent tuning (ticket: INC-1955600). putting owners: leah + maria + observability.

incident-bot: NOTE: PD routing and alert dedupe changes applied. suppression expires at 10m: 1955557389.

sanjay: handoff plan: i'm going offline in ~10m. leah take lead for next 2h. please run the checklist: 
- confirm customer acknowledgement
- keep dedupe & routing in place until 30m after p99 returns to baseline
- capture exact alert fingerprints and example traces in ticket
- schedule follow-up with product evaluation and cost/latency tradeoffs

leah: taking lead. i'll coordinate with alex to keep monitoring and with maria for dashboard updates. tagging @oncall-rotation so backup knows to escalate only if we get new distinct errors.

alex: system note: i added a temporary frontend rate-limit for anonymous clients hitting /v1/generate to throttle aggressive retry loops. config snippet: 
```
frontend.rate_limits.add({ route: "/v1/generate", key: "client_ip", limit: 100r/m, burst: 25 })
```
applied to edge fleet in us-east.

maria: finops note: throttling could increase latency for some valid requests; we'll capture tail latency and hit counts for the affected customers. adding metrics to the ticket.

leah: update at +12m: fintech-ops replied — they rolled out a retry change yesterday and are rolling it back now. they will coordinate a slower ramp. they did confirm spikes on their side.

sanjay: great. once their rollback stabilizes, we keep routing/dedupe for +30m then revert. create a short runbook entry for 'client retry storms' with playbook steps (dedupe, grouping, temporary threshold, contact customer).

maria: opened runbook PR: https://git.redwood/runs/alert-playbooks/PR-72 — includes checklist and dashboard links.

leah: logging the post-incident changes to the alerts tracking doc. action items: 
- (leah) revert dedupe & routing in 40m if stable
- (alex) track frontend throttle impact, revert if customer complaints
- (maria) finalize dashboard and postmortem notes for the weekly SRE review

oncall-rotation: acknowledged. will only escalate if new unique alert signature appears. please ping in this thread before making PD-wide changes.

incident-bot: REMINDER: suppression for misrouted-429 ends at 1955557389.

sanjay: handing off now. thanks team. :pray:

leah: copying timeline to the incident timeline doc and marking this thread for follow-up. will post summary in #incidents in 1h. :white_check_mark:

maria: summary posted and ticket INC-1955600 created with owners & links. leaving monitoring watch but stepping back to async.

alex: keeping an eye on queues for the next 30m. will report if anything changes.

leah: closing active paging loop for people on this channel. if you still get paged, escalate to pd-ops. thanks everyone.
